body.objective: Complete the tensor layer with presentation-independent abstract-index canonicalization and invariant contraction generation. Named-axis tensors and coordinate curvature now work, but Conflux cannot yet recognize that two curvature, current or anomaly expressions are the same after dummy-index relabeling, slot symmetries, Bianchi identities, metric moves or epsilon conventions. The first consumers are sf:program/work/black-hole-polar-composed-repair, sf:program/work/quantum-parity-odd-third-curvature-carrier-manifest and sf:program/work/observer-ward-cokernel-irrep-decomposition.
body.stop_condition: Provide typed abstract indices with bundle, variance, parity and grading; canonical dummy-index relabeling; mono-term slot symmetries through permutation groups/double cosets; multi-term Young/Bianchi relations; metric raising/lowering and trace handling; oriented epsilon contractions and dimension-dependent antisymmetrization; covariant derivative commutators to declared jet order; and orbit-first generation of scalar, tensor and current contractions. Emit canonical forms plus explicit permutation/relation witnesses, stabilizers and refusal boundaries. Demonstrate equality of independently written Ricci-to-Bach identities, reproduce one parity-odd C-cubed basis/quotient, and canonicalize one Lee-Wald current from action and component presentations. Compare against an independent xAct/Cadabra/Sage or separately implemented contraction-graph rail. Expose contraction graphs and canonical witnesses to Conflux so it can compare formulas without importing expected equality flags.
body.forbid: no component sampling used as a tensor identity proof; no implicit signature, Riemann, epsilon or symmetrization convention; no hash equality used as canonical-equivalence proof; no four-dimensional identity applied in generic dimension; no Bianchi relation trusted without a generated witness; no physics-specific Bach or anomaly basis embedded in lib/math; no producer normal form reused as the sole verifier
notes: Priority A. This closes the largest remaining presentation gap between tensor geometry and Conflux.
It should compose with tensor, curvature, wigner/harmonic, graph-hypergraph symmetry and the single-epsilon quotient work.
A bounded first slice may support Riemann/Weyl tensors and one covariant derivative in dimension four, while refusing unsupported Young types.
